title: Strict local invariant description of a finite group quotient
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and let a finite group $G$ act on $X$. Suppose $q:X\to Y$ is a finite surjective scheme quotient, with orbit-space topology and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$. Let $M$ be an fs log structure on $X$, preserved by $G$, and put $N=(q_*M)^G$, as a sheaf on the small etale site of $Y$. Then $Y$ is Noetherian and the geometric fibres of $q$ are the $G$-orbits. For a geometric point $\bar x$ of $X$, put $\bar y=q(\bar x)$, $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. The canonical map identifies $B$ with $A^H$, makes $A$ a finite $B$-algebra, and identifies $N_{\bar y}$ with $M_{\bar x}^H$, compatibly with structural maps to $B\hookrightarrow A$. These identifications respect the unit subgroups. Strict local rings and geometric stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]; finite means module-finite on affine opens [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; fs log structures are as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. No log regularity, triviality of the action on strata, or generic freeness is assumed.

source.place: Exposé VI, paragraph following Proposition 3.5, printed p.74, and opening of proof 3.7(b), p.75 (strict local quotient); underlying finite decomposition and flat invariants: Stacks Tags 04GH (algebra-lemma-finite-over-henselian), 0BRH (more-algebra-lemma-base-change-invariants).

proof.text: For an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset Y$, finiteness gives $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ finite as a $D$-module. The invariant structure-sheaf hypothesis identifies the structure map with $D=R^G\hookrightarrow R$. Since this inverse image is an affine open of the Noetherian scheme $X$, [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] makes $R$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-per-finite-quotient-noetherian-descent] to this injective finite map. Thus every such $D$ is Noetherian, so the affine opens of $Y$ form a covering by spectra of Noetherian rings, and $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: VI, quotient background after Proposition 3.5; Noetherian descent is the separately stated Eakin–Nagata input.

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is quasi-compact. Pull back any open covering of $Y$ to $X$, take a finite subcover there, and use surjectivity of $q$ to see that the corresponding finitely many opens cover $Y$. Thus $Y$ is quasi-compact, and together with Step 1 it is Noetherian. If $X$ is empty, surjectivity makes $Y$ empty and all remaining assertions about points are vacuous.

source.place: VI, finite quotient setting; elementary open-cover argument.

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}D$ containing its image, and $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Write $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. The affine-neighbourhood cofinality [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal] identifies the stalk colimit with the coordinate-ring colimit defining strict henselization, hence identifies this with $\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{Y,\bar y}$; the same identification applies on $X$. By [lem-sbc-affine-strict-henselization-structural-flat], $D\to B$ is flat, and by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality], $B$ is local. Put $C=B\otimes_D R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the canonical finite decomposition [lem-trf-finite-base-strict-localization],
$$C\cong\prod_{\bar x\in P(\bar y)} A_{\bar x},\qquad A_{\bar x}=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x},$$
where $P(\bar y)$ is the finite set of lifts with field $\Omega$, and each $A_{\bar x}$ is a finite local $B$-algebra. All maps are structural maps. The decomposition is $G$-equivariant: the action permutes the lifts, and its induced maps on strict localizations commute with the canonical decomposition maps.

source.place: Tags 03PS, 04HX, and 03QP proof; finite decomposition as in algebra.tex Tags 04GH and 05WR.

proof.text:
Compute the invariants without dividing by $|G|$. Since $D=R^G$, the sequence
$$0\longrightarrow D\longrightarrow R\xrightarrow{\delta}\bigoplus_{g\in G}R,\qquad \delta(r)=(g(r)-r)_g$$
is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with the flat $D$-module $B$. Tensor product commutes with this finite direct sum by its universal property, and the resulting difference map on $C$ is $(g(c)-c)_g$. Its kernel is $C^G$, so the canonical map identifies $B=C^G$ as rings, including injectivity.

source.place: Tag 0BRH (lemma-base-change-invariants), first paragraph of proof, written out as the kernel of the finite difference map.

proof.text: The action of $G$ on $P(\bar y)$ is transitive. It is nonempty whenever $\bar y$ exists: otherwise the product in Step 3 is the zero ring, contradicting the injection of the nonzero local ring $B$ in Step 4. If there were two orbits, the tuple equal to $1$ on one orbit and $0$ elsewhere would be a nontrivial idempotent in $C^G=B$. A local ring has no such idempotent: for $e^2=e$, one of $e,1-e$ is a unit, forcing $e=1$ or $e=0$. This proves the geometric-fibre assertion, including nonreduced fibres, since the index set in Step 3 is precisely the set of geometric points of the fibre.

source.place: Tags 0BRH and 0BRI (lemma-one-orbit); elementary idempotent proof after finite strict-local decomposition.

proof.text: Fix $\bar x\in P(\bar y)$, let $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$ and $A=A_{\bar x}$. Evaluation at $\bar x$ gives $C^G\to A^H$. Its inverse sends $a\in A^H$ to the tuple whose component at $g\bar x$ is $g(a)$. This is well-defined because two choices of $g$ differ by an element of $H$, and the tuple is $G$-invariant. The two maps are inverse ring maps. Together with Step 4 this identifies the canonical map $B\to A$ with $B\simeq A^H\hookrightarrow A$. Finiteness of $A$ over $B$ was supplied by Step 3.

source.place: VI, paragraph after Proposition 3.5 and 3.7(b), opening strict-local reduction; explicit invariant-tuple calculation.

proof.text:
Taking invariants of a sheaf is a finite limit, namely the equalizer of the diagonal and action maps to its $G$-fold product. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-stalk-finite-limits] to $q_*M$: it gives $N_{\bar y}=((q_*M)_{\bar y})^G$. The natural restriction bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-finite-pushforward-stalk] identifies the latter stalk with $\prod_{\bar z\in P(\bar y)}M_{\bar z}$. These restriction maps preserve monoid operations and are $G$-equivariant, since restrictions commute with the action maps. Consequently
$$N_{\bar y}\cong\left(\prod_{\bar z\in P(\bar y)}M_{\bar z}\right)^G.$$

source.place: Tag 03QP (proposition-finite-higher-direct-image-zero), part (1), with finite-limit preservation of geometric stalks.

proof.text: Apply the same tuple formula as in Step 6 to the monoids in Step 7: an $H$-fixed $m\in M_{\bar x}$ determines the invariant tuple with component $g(m)$ at $g\bar x$, independently of the representative $g$. Evaluation at $\bar x$ is its inverse. Thus $N_{\bar y}\simeq M_{\bar x}^H$ canonically. The structural map is componentwise and commutes with every action map; evaluating at $\bar x$ therefore gives the commutative square with the canonical $B\hookrightarrow A$ of Step 6.

source.place: VI, paragraph after Proposition 3.5: invariant log structure; explicit evaluation and structural-map compatibility.

proof.text: Finally, $(A^\times)^H=(A^H)^\times$: the inverse in $A$ of an invariant unit is invariant, and the reverse inclusion is immediate. The log-structure axiom identifies $M_{\bar x}^\times$ with $A^\times$, equivariantly. Likewise a tuple of units is invertible componentwise, and the inverse of an invariant tuple is invariant. The evaluations above therefore restrict to the same unit subgroups, identifying them with $B^\times$. No tameness, log regularity, or freeness hypothesis entered the argument.

source.place: VI, invariant log structure after Proposition 3.5; elementary inverse calculation.

proof_origin.place: VI, paragraph following Proposition 3.5 and opening of 3.7(b), justified under the stated general hypotheses by Stacks Tags 0BRH, 04GH, 05WR and 03QP, plus Eakin–Nagata descent.
